messages:
maya: Heads-up, saw a big regression after the stream-coordinator rollout (v0.9.4). 8-GPU TP+PP jobs showing repeated stalls during cudagraph replay when KV cache prefetch is enabled. Latency spikes ~1.1-1.6s per batch. trace pasted below. :eyes:

maya: log snippet:
```
[GPU0] replay: start cudagraph_replay(stream=stream_worker_2)
[GPU0] kernel_select -> selected kernel=matmul_int8_fast, requires_host_probe=true
[GPU0] HOST_SYNC: cudaStreamSynchronize(stream_probe)
[GPU0] replay: launch graph on stream_worker_2
[GPU0] allreduce: waiting for peers (delayed start 1.2ms)
```

samir: Which commit/PR? can you repro locally?

maya: rollback is easy to repro. rollup PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/stream-coordinator/pulls/412 (merge 2026-03-16). repro steps:
```
# repro: 8 GPUs, TP=2 PP=4, batch=8, kv_prefetch=true, cudagraph_replay=true
./loadgen --model gpt-13b --gpus 0-7 --tp 2 --pp 4 --batch 8 --kv-prefetch on --cudagraph-replay on
```

jen: ack. can you run nsight or nvprof and share a timeline? also try with KV prefetch off to see if it's related to KV warmup. nvtx spans would help.

maya: attached a short nsight export (trimmed). main findings: replay right after host sync blocks the worker stream and delays all-reduce kickoff on other devices. The host_sync shows up only when kernel_select picked the int8 kernel variant. If kernel_selector picks fp16 path, we don't see the sync.

kai: ran a quick perf run. numbers: average all-reduce start latency (time between expected allreduce start and actual start): baseline: 0.15ms, after rollout: 1.35ms (std 0.4). throughput down ~7%. This matches your 1.2ms. Happens when kvcache prefetch populates and cudagraph_replay is used.

samir: so hypothesis: kernel probe path invokes a synchronous host call (cudaStreamSynchronize) to query kernel attributes which blocks the stream used by cudagraph replay, causing peer GPUs to stall waiting on the communication phase. Why did that change in stream-coordinator?

maya: PR introduced a "probe-and-pin" optimization where we probe kernels at runtime and pin them for reuse. probe path added a sync to ensure kernel introspection before graph capture. Looks cheap in single-GPU tests but in multi-GPU it serializes the replay window.

jen: 2 quick mitigations to test: 1) move probe off the critical replay path and do it lazily on a background stream, using cudaEventRecord + cudaStreamWaitEvent rather than cudaStreamSynchronize; 2) skip probe when running within graph replay (we can annotate replay sessions).

kai: i tried toggling quantized_kernel_prefer=false (fall back to fp16 kernels) and stalls vanish. So it's definitely kernel variant + probe interaction.

maya: exact repro config + minimal log attached. also observed that disabling KV prefetch reduces but doesn't fully eliminate the delay (KV prefetch amplifies it by shifting timings so probe happens right before allreduce).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: stream-coordinator v0.9.4 rolled out to staging at 2026-03-16T22:10Z by ci/cd. Can trigger a rollback via `/deploy stream-coordinator v0.9.3 --staging`

samir: plan: revert the probe sync change for canary, and implement the event-based probe as a follow-up. can someone prepare a minimal patch?

jen: gonna draft a quick patch. snippet idea:
```
// instead of cudaStreamSynchronize(probe_stream);
cudaEvent_t ev; cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&ev, cudaEventDisableTiming);
cudaEventRecord(ev, probe_stream);
cudaStreamWaitEvent(replay_stream, ev, 0);
// now safe to launch replay without blocking host
```

maya: thanks. can you also add a unit/integration test that runs a small cudagraph replay + mock kernel probe under 4xGPU and asserts no host sync is executed? we should catch regressions.

kai: i'll run the patched build across our infra (TP=2 PP=4, TP=4 PP=2, and single-GPU) and report perf numbers tomorrow. i'll also try a canary rollout to dedicated.

samir: assign: jen -> patch + test, kai -> multi-GPU perf runs, maya -> create minimal repro harness and benchmark scripts. i'll coordinate rollback if numbers don't improve.

maya: noted. next steps PR: #416 (patch) and #417 (test + canary). tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :thumbsup:

jen: sending initial PR in ~2h.

kai: running perf now, will post timeline.

maya: thanks all.
